escena: SCENE (art direction pass, studio in Bogota, morning, NO faces): THE SUBJECT OF THE PHOTOGRAPH IS THE CORRECTION, NOT THE HAND THAT MADE IT — verify it by these landmarks: a printed proof fills the whole frame, seen at a steep angle so its paper grain and ink-blue halftone rosette are razor sharp; drawn ON TOP of it in thick ORANGE grease pencil are the marks of a review — a circle around one element, an arrow dragging it across, a firm crossing-out, a bracket in the margin. Those ORANGE marks are the SHARPEST, most deliberate, most contrasted thing in the picture and the eye lands on them first. The grease pencil itself lies on the sheet where it was put down; ANY hand is at most a blurred fragment leaving the frame at the far edge, never the subject. Hard window light rakes across the sheet so the waxy ridge of each pencil stroke throws its own tiny shadow and reads as physical material. 100mm macro at f/5.6. Everything is completely unbranded, no readable text anywhere — the marks are marks, not letters.

lecho.objeto: the out-of-focus near edge of the dark walnut worktop under the sheet
